title: Corrupt darkMode value in localStorage white-screens the entire app
description: JSON.parse(getLocalData('darkMode')) runs unguarded inside a useState initializer, i.e. during the render phase of the provider that wraps the whole app. A non-JSON persisted value throws out of the root render with no error boundary above it, blanking the SPA on every reload until site data is cleared by hand.
test: src/context/ThemeContext.logic.test.ts::BUG-003: survives a non-JSON darkMode value in localStorage instead of failing to render
observed: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'o', "not-json" is not valid JSON
expected: provider renders children and defaults to light mode
fix: wrap the parse in try/catch, fall back to false, and optionally remove the bad key

title: Admin search values containing '=' are silently truncated
description: getUrl splits each queryParameter with String.split('=') and destructures [name, value], discarding everything after the second '='. FhirApi.getUrl does the same job correctly with indexOf('=')+substring. Reachable via SearchContainer -> SearchFormQuery.getQueryParameters() -> manageExport.tsx:49; the _source field is appended for every resource type and its values are URLs that legally contain '='. The admin console runs a different query than the operator typed and presents the result as the answer.
test: src/api/adminApi.test.ts::BUG-001: preserves a parameter value that itself contains "=" instead of truncating it
fix: split on the first '=' only, as FhirApi.getUrl does, and skip entries with no '='

title: Providers configured without OIDC discovery can never authenticate
description: The `if (!wellKnownUrl) throw` guard sits after the else branch that exists specifically to handle !wellKnownUrl, so the explicit AUTHORIZE_URL/TOKEN_URL/LOGOUT_URL configuration mode is dead code. The thrown message also names LOGOUT_URL (copy-paste from the guard above), so an operator who set all three variables correctly is told LOGOUT_URL is missing. Config-gated: every documented deployment sets WELL_KNOWN_URL, which is why this has not been hit.
test: src/utils/authUrlProvider.test.ts::BUG-002: resolves from AUTHORIZE_URL/TOKEN_URL/LOGOUT_URL when no WELL_KNOWN_URL is set
observed: rejected with Error: REACT_APP_AUTH_TESTIDP_LOGOUT_URL is not defined
expected: resolves with the three configured URLs
fix: delete the if (!wellKnownUrl) guard; wellKnownUrl is already optional in the declared return type

title: A resource-existence checkmark is shown for a reference that was never queried
description: When new props short-circuit the fetch (no resourceType or no queryParameters) the effect returns without resetting count/atLimit/isLoading/error, so the hook reports the previous query's count as a settled, error-free answer. Reachable because Reference.tsx:37 renders ReferenceLink with key={index}, so React reuses the instance when the reference array changes; a reference with no '/' yields id undefined -> queryParameters undefined -> early return. ReferenceLink then renders its green 'Resource exists' checkmark for a reference the app never checked.
test: src/hooks/useResourceCount.test.ts::BUG-004: clears a previous count when the new props short-circuit the fetch
observed: count === 1 (previous query's value) with isLoading false and error null
fix: reset count/atLimit/error in the short-circuit branch before returning

title: Okta: the PKCE code_verifier survives a failed token exchange
description: removeLocalData('code_verifier') sits inside the try after the awaited token POST, so it is skipped on any failure, while the catch block is a bare `catch (error) { throw error; }`. RFC 7636 makes the verifier single-use; after a failed exchange it stays in localStorage indefinitely, readable by any script on the origin and by anyone with access to the browser profile.
test: src/services/OktaAuthService.test.ts::BUG-005: consumes the verifier even when the token exchange fails
observed: localStorage still holds 'stored-verifier' after the exchange rejects
fix: move removeLocalData('code_verifier') into a finally block
retraction_reason: Retracted as OVERSTATED by adversarial review: the behavior is real but it is not a defect. getLoginUrlAsync unconditionally mints a fresh verifier on every login attempt (proven by the file's own passing test at OktaAuthService.test.ts:105) and logout() clears code_verifier via removeAuthData, so the stale value survives only until the next login or logout; a verifier is inert without its matching authorization code, which is already spent or expired in every listed failure scenario; and RFC 7636 forbids reuse across authorization requests - which this code never does - not retention in client storage after a failed exchange. Reclassified as a code-hygiene note in Suspicious Pattern 5 of domain-invariants.md; the proving test named above was deleted. Line kept for provenance only.

title: Cognito: the PKCE code_verifier survives a failed token exchange
description: Identical defect and shape to BUG-005 in a second, independent copy of the token-exchange code. Filed separately because the two services do not share the path and each needs its own fix.
test: src/services/CognitoAuthService.test.ts::BUG-006: consumes the verifier even when the token exchange fails
observed: localStorage still holds 'stored-verifier' after the exchange rejects
fix: move removeLocalData('code_verifier') into a finally block; consider hoisting the duplicated PKCE block into a shared base
retraction_reason: Retracted as OVERSTATED by adversarial review, byte-identical reasoning to BUG-005 (including the disproving sibling test at CognitoAuthService.test.ts:128, 'mints a fresh verifier and challenge on every login attempt'): a verifier is inert without its authorization code, the next login attempt overwrites it, logout clears it, and RFC 7636 forbids reuse across authorization requests rather than post-failure retention in storage. Reclassified as a code-hygiene note in Suspicious Pattern 5 of domain-invariants.md; the proving test named above was deleted. Line kept for provenance only.

title: API Console streams a body that disagrees with the response received
description: sendRequest wraps onChunk in its own TextDecoder used with {stream:true} but never makes the final argument-less decode() call that BaseApi.streamRequest (baseApi.ts:249) and BaileyApi.streamChat (baileyApi.ts:60-63) both make. For a body ending mid-multi-byte-character - a truncated or dropped response, which this stack explicitly supports via incomplete:true - the streamed text loses the trailing bytes while rawText keeps them, so the API Console displays a body that differs from the response actually received.
test: src/api/fhirApi.test.ts::BUG-007: delivers the whole body through onChunk, flushing the decoder at the end
fix: after streamRequest resolves: const flushed = decoder.decode(); if (flushed) { onChunk?.(flushed); }
